focus: What a default-on integration needs, cost and risk: reader, cadence, label lifecycle, qualification, record, risk register
noveltyJustification: Integration shape, label-lifecycle conclusion, widened-qualification need and risk register are new synthesis; constraints inherited from iterations 1-4
keyQuestions: Q5: What would a default-on integration need, and at what cost and risk?

title: A documented surface exists but no reader: needs a named consumer (README check row) and an advisory-only action policy
Cost: minutes per run today (census ~171s, draw ~381s, model 41s); model cost flat in corpus size; periodic advisory feasible, per-commit not
Label lifecycle is the operational bottleneck: draw refuses override, rows pin commits, gate needs all 20 live rows labeled; sustainable shape is frozen benchmark + explicit re-draws
Qualification must widen beyond provider/model to instruction hash, keep rule, window/rerun config and row set
A reader needs per-row outcomes and the kind split; today the report is aggregate-only
Risk register: claim-less rows, threshold flips, silent skips, doc-text leakage, untested sign/flip branches, moving surface (Deem removal), no zero-call value

Recommended shape: advisory periodic benchmark-anchored scan with prefilter, aggregation fix, per-kind/per-row record, widened requalification, tests, and expansion only after an illustrative classifier

direction: Wire the scan into the pre-commit hook
reason: Cost: minutes per run today; per-commit cadence is infeasible; the model arm needs labels and a credential
